headline: The Planning Board opened hearings on a proposed Coslin Drive Costco, while town committees prepared for upcoming Special Town Meeting articles and FY28 budget planning.
synopsis: The Planning Board opened a public hearing on a proposal for a 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 15-pump fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive, reviewing site designs and traffic impacts before continuing the hearing to October 19. In preparation for the October 17 Special Town Meeting, the Trails Committee evaluated fallback floor amendments for Peninsula Trail bridge funding following non-recommendation votes by the Select Board and Advisory Committee. The Planning Board also continued its hearing on a two-family dwelling zoning warrant article to the morning of Special Town Meeting. Meanwhile, the Southborough School Committee initiated its FY28 operating budget process under municipal guidance requiring both level-service and level-funded scenarios.

highlights.title: Costco warehouse and fuel station proposal hearing
highlights.why: The Planning Board opened public review of a 167,000-square-foot store and gas station spanning Southborough and Westborough, focusing on site access and traffic generation. The hearing was continued to October 19 pending consultant traffic reviews.

highlights.title: Peninsula Trail bridge Town Meeting funding strategy
highlights.why: With the Select Board and Advisory Committee not recommending CPA funding for Article 4, the committee debated drafting a floor amendment to reduce new CPA requests to $25,000 by repurposing existing funds.

highlights.title: Two-family dwelling zoning bylaw hearing
highlights.why: The Planning Board examined revised warrant language regarding two-family homes and debated whether to sponsor floor amendments regarding lot sizes in commercial districts before continuing the hearing to October 17.

highlights.title: FY28 school operating budget process and timeline
highlights.why: The Southborough School Committee began preparations for the FY28 budget, reviewing municipal directives to present both level-service and level-funded models while tracking inflation and volatile out-of-district special education costs.
